title: Verify identity
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Check the mission record and ask a person to bind track identity. A claimed vehicle ID is not permission.

title: Restricted area permission
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Review the specific zone permission and mission window. Presence without confirmed permission requires human review, not an inference of intent.

title: Predictive human handoff
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Present the trajectory, observation age, model assumptions and estimated entry time to the watch officer. Record acknowledgment without changing measured risk.

title: Approaching a zone
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Verify permission while the mean path approaches a relevant zone. A forecast is conditional on constant velocity and assumed noise.

title: Hazard occupancy
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Hand off a fresh observed hazard-zone occupancy to a human. Mission authorization does not eliminate physical hazard.

title: Uncertain proximity
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Ask for a fresh position when the current uncertainty envelope overlaps a relevant zone. The envelope is not certified coverage.

title: Lost or stale position
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Show loss of coverage and retain outstanding human handoffs. A source heartbeat never refreshes vehicle position.

title: Conflicting measurements
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Ask for reliable fresh observations. Preserve rejected measurements in audit history; do not teleport the accepted track.

title: Persistent route deviation
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Ask a known operator about persistent measured route deviation. No message is sent automatically.

title: Expected communication missing
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Use the cooperative mission reporting interval. Unknown non-cooperative objects do not have an assumed heartbeat obligation.

title: Routine monitoring
text: Synthetic demonstration procedure. Continue observations and reassess when evidence changes. LOW is not a guarantee of safety.
